payload.title: Same-Sex Marriage in Greece and What Couples Need
payload.excerpt: As at November 2026, same-sex marriage in Greece is legal: Greek law allows a civil marriage between two persons of different or the same sex, and the change has been in force since 16 February 2024.
key_takeaways: Since 16 February 2024, Greek law has allowed civil marriage between two persons of the same sex, and the reform covers civil marriage, not religious ceremonies.
Ask the municipality where you marry for its document list, and Rhodes, for example, asks for a certificate of no impediment naming your partner.
The Australian Embassy in Athens issues Certificates of No Impediment, and same-sex marriages that took place overseas are generally recognised in Australia.
Choose a venue that tells you plainly it hosts same-sex weddings, and ask how the civil ceremony and the celebration fit together on the day.

faq.q: Is same-sex marriage legal in Greece?
faq.a: Yes. As at November 2026, Law 5089/2024 allows civil marriage between two persons of different or the same sex, in force since 16 February 2024. It is a civil marriage, not a religious one.

faq.q: Can foreigners get married in Greece as a same-sex couple?
faq.a: The law does not set out how a foreign national's freedom to marry is assessed, so ask the municipality where you marry which documents it needs. The Municipality of Rhodes, for example, asks for a certificate of no impediment naming your partner, passports, a joint application and a fee. Confirm with your municipality and the Australian Embassy in Athens, including any fees.

faq.q: Do we need to live in Greece to marry there?
faq.a: The law itself states no residency condition. Ask the municipality where you will marry what it requires of two non-resident Australians, and check with the Australian Embassy in Athens.

faq.q: Is a same-sex marriage in Greece recognised in Australia?
faq.a: Same-sex marriages that took place overseas are generally recognised in Australia. It is generally recognised if it was valid under Greek law when it took place and would have been valid under Australian law had it taken place here. Check with the authorities if you have any doubt.

faq.q: Can same-sex couples marry in a Greek Orthodox church?
faq.a: The law leaves churches free to set their own conditions for religious ceremonies. The Greek Orthodox Archdiocese of Australia describes its sacrament of marriage as the union of a man and a woman.

Smartraveller says same-sex relationships are legal in Greece, though attitudes vary throughout the country, and are generally more accepting on islands such as Mykonos, Santorini and Ios. Homophobic attacks have occurred.

faq.q: Can we have a symbolic same-sex wedding in Santorini or Mykonos?
faq.a: Yes, a symbolic ceremony carries no legal paperwork, so it is a matter between you and your venue. Ask the venue in writing whether it hosts same-sex weddings and who can lead the ceremony.
